identity.title: HU promotes fidelity and leader-repeat integration during CRISPR adaptation in the type III-A system of Thermotoga profunda.

content.abstract: CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity relies on the acquisition of foreign DNA fragments as spacers within CRISPR arrays. Although spacer integration is generally catalysed by the conserved Cas1-Cas2 integrase complex, accurate integration frequently requires accessory factors. In the type I-E CRISPR-Cas system of Escherichia coli, the DNA-binding protein integration host factor (IHF) promotes leader-proximal spacer acquisition. The DNA bending properties of IHF exerted at the CRISPR locus are thought to form the mechanistic basis for the supportive function of IHF. However, many organisms lack IHF posing the questions how integration specificity is achieved in these organisms and whether analogous host factors contribute to adaptation in other CRISPR-Cas systems. Here, we investigated spacer integration in the type III-A CRISPR-Cas system of the hyperthermophilic bacterium Thermotoga profunda. Using reconstituted in vitro integration assays, we show that the TpCas1-TpCas2 complex alone exhibits limited integration fidelity and generates substantial off-target integration events. We identify the highly conserved histone-like protein HU (TpHU) as a critical cofactor for accurate spacer acquisition. Addition of TpHU strongly promotes integration at the leader-repeat junction while suppressing erroneous integration into noncanonical sites. TpHU therefore acts as a determinant of integration fidelity and target-site selection during adaptation.
